[cable-satellite-tv] ROSTER BACKFILL 2026-09-30 (task roster-backfill-cable-satellite-tv, edited in place; change log in categories/roster-backfill-cable-satellite-tv.json). Totals now: 234 entries, 76 detailed, 158 roster, and 56 roster rows still without a website (151 before this pass). (1) Upgraded 40 roster operators to detailed. These are the largest remaining cable, municipal and co-op TV billers by approximate video footprint: Shentel cable, Glo Fiber, Comporium, Hotwire/Fision, Summit Broadband, ALLO, HBC, CDE Lightband, BTES, Cedar Falls Utilities, HTC, GVTC, Golden West, GTA, DOCOMO PACIFIC, Claro PR, ImOn, Conway Corp, Zito Media, Antietam, Swyft, Truvista, Frankfort Plant Board, Murray Electric, Glasgow EPB, Scottsboro EPB, GEUS, Wyandotte, Easton Utilities/Velocity, SELCO Shrewsbury, Lightcurve, CassComm, Hood Canal, TVS Cablenet/Thacker-Grigsby, Long Lines, Wadsworth CityLink, Boycom, Nelsonville TV, CNSNext Thomasville and Algona Municipal Utilities. Each detailed entry has pay, autopay and bill-history links taken from the official site this session (Zendesk/Salesforce sitemaps and APIs were used where pages are JavaScript-only), phones, payment processor, assistance programs, and a note on how to drop or downgrade the TV package. Duplicate rows in internet-rural-coops.json, internet-national-regional.json, landline-telcos.json and the electric/water files are cross-referenced in each note. (2) TV status corrections: Cedar Falls Utilities ends TV on 2026-10-11; Fayetteville Public Utilities (TN) ended cable TV on 2021-12-31; Riviera Utilities, Columbia Power & Water and Coldwater BPU no longer list a TV product; Adams CATV now redirects to Blue Ridge, Keene Valley Video to SLIC Fiber, Belzoni Cable to Southeast Broadband, WEHCO/Longview Cable to Cablelynx Broadband, and Inter-Mountain Cable to Gearheart; San Bruno CityNet's page is gone. Many operators have moved from QAM cable to app-based streaming TV (Shentel TV, SELCO Stream, CityLink View, NextStream, dTV+, Flight Video, Swyft TV). (3) Websites: about 95 previously empty or weak roster rows were given official sites. Method: exact-name cross-reference against every other category file and rosters/telecom_providers.csv, then about 3,900 name-derived candidate domains resolved by DNS, homepages fetched, and accepted only when the title or body matched the operator's distinctive name and the service area. Every accepted match was hand-reviewed and false positives were rejected (PR agencies, foreign ISPs, parked domains). Sites that answered only with bot challenges (Cloudflare 403, HTTP 202, Vercel 429) are recorded with verified=false. Checked against: rosters/telecom_cable_operators.csv (FCC Form 477 Jun-2021 cable holding companies + ACA Connects/NCTA flags) and the Leichtman/Wikipedia MSO table (previous pass). STILL MISSING: about 56 very small systems (mostly under 20,000 people covered) have no confirmable site, e.g. Cable TV of East Alabama, Country Cablevision, Access Cable, Bee Line Cable, Jefferson County Cable, Limestone Cable, Spring City Cable, Wire Tele-View, Somerfield, Belhaven, Ocracoke, Bridger, Tongue River and Iron River TV. Many probably bill by mail only or have closed. FCC COALS (Form 322) and the ACA Connects member directory both blocked our fetcher (403), and WebSearch quota was exhausted this pass. The next pass should use COALS community-unit contacts or web search for these names. Previous-pass notes still apply: the vMVPDs and the top-15 MVPDs were detailed in the first pass, and Cox is combining with Charter/Spectrum. Industry notes: Florida 55+/HOA communities (Hotwire, Summit, Blue Stream, Smartaira, Laguna Woods/West Coast Internet in CA) often bill TV through HOA dues, which a resident cannot drop individually. REVIEW PASS 2026-10-02 (skeptical second pass, task roster-backfill-cable-satellite-tv): Totals now 234 entries, 78 detailed, 156 roster, 56 roster rows still without a website. (a) Link check: every website/login/help/link URL on all detailed entries (448 unique URLs) was re-requested with curl; no hard 404s were found. Non-200 results were bot walls or JS apps (DIRECTV, Liberty PR, Fubo and Blue Stream 403; Summit and Blue Ridge Zendesk 403, which the Zendesk API can read; Optimum and Spectrum timeouts), not dead pages. Page titles of the 200 responses were scanned for soft-404s, and none were found. (b) Content re-read and fixes on these entries: Breezeline (help center moved to help.breezeline.com; all links updated; autopay_cancel and statements filled; payment-arrangement assistance link), Mediacom (autopay terms and statements login filled; /support pages 404), Armstrong (statements login and caregiver account-roles article), Service Electric Cablevision (customer service phone, PO Box mail address, statements), Sparklight (Payment History article; change/cancel-service article for dropping TV), Frontier (pay-by-phone 800-917-7489, mail address, customer service phone, affordability programs; contact page now says Frontier has joined Verizon), altafiber (phone and Fioptics Internet Assistance/Lifeline), WOW (pay-by-phone 1-866-496-9669), Ritter (autopay_cancel, Lifeline, phone), Shentel cable and Glo Fiber (autopay_setup and statements article URLs from the official support sitemap; Glo Fiber website corrected to glofiber.com), GTA (pay-by-phone and eBill login), Vyve (Essentials Connect low-income plan), TG/TVS (support page confirms billing is portal or phone only). (c) Completeness: rosters/telecom_cable_operators.csv (cable and fiber provider types) was compared with this file. Two TV billers that were missing were added as detailed: Muscatine Power and Water TV/MachLink (IA, still sells TV) and The Community Agency (TCA, O'Brien County IA, city-owned streaming video). Other unmatched roster rows are fixed-wireless or internet-only ISPs (Bluespan, Wired or Wireless, WindSpeed, KwiKom, PogoZone), or telco co-ops whose IPTV billing is already in internet-rural-coops.json and landline-telcos.json (Polar, Blue Valley, Rainbow, Panora/Guthrie, Star Telephone). These were not duplicated here. (d) Removed: Adams CATV (merged into Blue Ridge; note added to the Blue Ridge entry) and Fayetteville Public Utilities TN (FPU ended cable TV after 2021-12-31; its utility and internet billing stays in internet-rural-coops.json). Known remaining gaps: Hotwire/Fision, DOCOMO PACIFIC, Zito Media, Vyve, Hood Canal, Nelsonville and Wadsworth CityLink publish no public autopay or bill-history how-to pages; their help centers are JS-only or portal-only, so those link fields stay null. Riviera Utilities, Columbia Power & Water and Coldwater BPU are kept as roster rows, but no TV product was found on their sites. Users there should confirm on their bills.

[dental-vision-hearing] Checked completeness against: (1) Delta Dental's 39-company network — every state/territory is mapped to a Delta company entry (DDIC/Delta Dental of California enterprise covers CA, AL, FL, GA, LA, MS, MT, NV, TX, UT, NY, PA, MD, DE, WV, DC; separate companies for the rest; MN covers NE/ND; MO covers SC; Northeast Delta covers ME/NH/VT; NJ covers CT; Moda runs OR/AK; plus Puerto Rico; Hawaii Dental Service for HI). (2) Major national dental/vision carriers and the senior-marketed direct-to-consumer brands (AARP Dental, AARP Vision, Physicians Mutual, Spirit/Denali via Ameritas, Humana, Mutual of Omaha, Cigna). (3) Largest DSOs by office count (Heartland, Aspen, PDS, Smile Brands, Affordable Care, Dental Care Alliance, Western/Sonrava, Great Expressions, Mortenson, Coast, Midwest, 42 North, Tend, Dental365). (4) Largest optical chains (National Vision, EssilorLuxottica, MyEyeDr., Visionworks, Walmart/Costco/Sam's, Clarkson, Eyemart, Stanton) and hearing networks (Amplifon/Miracle-Ear/HearUSA, Demant/HearingLife, Sonova/AudioNova, GN/Beltone/Jabra, WSA/hear.com, Starkey/Audibel, TruHearing, UHC Hearing, NationsHearing, Costco/Sam's). Method: every URL came from the biller's own sitemap or from links on fetched pages; pages were fetched this session and text-extracted. Most insurers keep premium payment, autopay and statement history behind member logins, so public 'how-to' pages exist only for some (Delta Dental of California, AARP Dental, Humana, Anthem, Aspen, Coast, Great Expressions, Midwest, MyEyeDr., HearingLife, UHC Hearing). Where links.* is null, no public page was found — the member portal is the path. RUN 2 (2026-09-29): added/upgraded billing detail using web search plus direct fetch/curl. Key finding: individual & family plans for many Delta companies (WA, CO, VA, IL, MA, MO/SC, ME/NH/VT and others) are sold and billed through DeltaDentalCoversMe.com, run by Delta Dental of Wisconsin's Wyssta Services. Pay online or by autopay in the CoversMe account, by phone at 888-899-3734, or by mail to P.O. Box 1237, Wisconsin Rapids, WI 54495. Tennessee individual plans are administered by Morgan-White; Idaho, South Dakota, North Carolina and Arizona individual premium rules were read from each company's own FAQ. Added regional DSOs (Absolute Dental NV, Perfect Teeth NM/AZ/CO, Familia, Risas, Dental Depot OK, Comfort Dental), hearing networks and programs (Audibel, EPIC Hearing, Hearing Care Solutions->TruHearing, Start Hearing, Lexie, Starkey Cares Hear Now), Dentegra, Vision Source, EyeCare Partners, and the LensCrafters Credit Card (Synchrony). Upgraded Heartland (paymydentist.com e-statements), PDS (Smile Generation MyChart), Amplifon (CardPointe pay page), Aflac, Physicians Mutual, Mutual of Omaha, Guardian Direct, Sunbit, Cherry, CareCredit (mail address), Allegro, Proceed and HDS. STILL MISSING: several sites blocked automated fetch (403/Cloudflare): Visionworks, Physicians Mutual, LensCrafters, Walmart and Warby Parker, Davis Vision, Delta Dental of Oklahoma, NationsHearing, Nano Hearing, Specsavers, Zenni. Their facts came from search snippets and are marked verified=false. JS-rendered pages whose content could not be read: VSP and EyeMed member FAQs, United Concordia help center, Guardian billing FAQ, DeltaDentalCoversMe billing pages, Delta Dental of Minnesota shop. Premium autopay cancellation steps are rarely public; for most insurers, cancel autopay in the member portal or by phone. The web-search budget ran out mid-run, so the second-tier DSOs (Sage, Smile Brands sub-brands beyond Bright Now/Castle/Monarch, Benevis, Gentle Dental West) and the state Blue Cross Blue Shield standalone dental plans are not enumerated. Dental365's old domain is now for sale and its current site is unconfirmed. Independent dentists, optometrists and audiologists can't be enumerated: point users to the pay link or Payment ID on their statement (common portals: pay.yourdentistoffice.com, paymydentist.com, Cedar, Epic MyChart, CardPointe), or to the CareCredit provider locator. entries.name: LifeMed Alaska Membership
entries.parent_company: LifeMed Alaska (aviation services provided by Air Methods and others per site footer)
entries.service_area_detail: Statewide Alaska air medevac
entries.phone_customer_service: Billing (907) 249-8360; billing@lifemedalaska.com
entries.notes: Join/renew via eServices membership portal linked from the membership-pricing page (https://lifemedalaska.com/emergency-medical-transportation/membership-pricing/). Members face no out-of-pocket costs when transported by LifeMed. Medevac bills paid at https://admin.eservicestech.com/paymybill/lifemedalaska . MEDICARE: Part B covers medically necessary emergency air ambulance (80% of the approved amount after the Part B deductible); Medigap or a Medicare Advantage plan usually covers most of the rest, and the federal No Surprises Act (2022) bars out-of-network air-ambulance balance billing for insured patients. Medicare does NOT pay for or reimburse the membership fee. Memberships are not insurance and Medicaid enrollees generally may not buy them.

entries.name: KerixHealth (formerly Nextera Healthcare) direct primary care
entries.service_area_detail: Direct & advanced primary care clinics (Colorado origin) for individuals and employers
entries.senior_programs: Flat monthly fee; no copays for primary care.
entries.notes: FAQ: after the initial period you may cancel any time with 30 days' notice through your account portal; already-paid fees not refunded or prorated. Medicare eligibility depends on the clinician (physicians must opt out of Medicare to offer DPC). MEDICARE: Direct primary care (DPC) practices usually do not bill insurance; to accept a DPC fee from a Medicare patient the physician typically must opt out of Medicare, so neither the DPC fee nor visits there are paid by Medicare, and the patient signs a private contract. The patient keeps Medicare (Part A/B/D and any Medigap/Advantage) for specialists, hospitals, labs and imaging outside the practice. Since 2026 (2025 law) DPC fees up to $150/month individual can be paid from an HSA, but people enrolled in Medicare cannot contribute to an HSA. REVIEW 2026-10-02: FAQ re-read: flat monthly fee varying by location; new memberships must stay active 3 months, then cancel any time with 30 days notice through the account portal; paid fees are not refunded or prorated. HSA debit cards eligible from Jan 1, 2026. MEDICARE: participating physicians must opt out of Medicare to offer DPC to Medicare patients; you keep Medicare but those doctors cannot bill it, so Medicare will not pay for their visits.

entries.name: Pinellas County Sunstar FirstCare Ambulance Membership (FL)
entries.service_area_detail: Pinellas County (St. Petersburg, Clearwater, Largo); calendar year
entries.phone_customer_service: (727) 582-2008 press 1; Safety & Emergency Services (727) 464-3835
entries.senior_programs: 2026 fees $89 single / $133 family. Covers deductibles and copays for medically necessary Sunstar transports within Pinellas County; uninsured members get 20% off. No cards issued.
entries.notes: Covers 100% of deductibles and copays and 50% of medically necessary trips insurance denies; uninsured members get 20% off. Applications at pinellas.gov/firstcare; must be received before year-end for a Jan 1 start. Ambulance bills: https://pinellas.gov/services/pay-an-ambulance-bill/ (Sunstar bill pay https://pay.bill2pay.com/client/PNLSEMS). A large senior population makes this one of the biggest county programs in Florida. MEDICARE: Part B covers medically necessary emergency ground ambulance (80% of the approved amount after the Part B deductible; non-emergency trips only with a doctor's certification); Medigap usually pays the 20%. The federal No Surprises Act does NOT protect against ground-ambulance balance bills. Medicare, Medigap and Medicare Advantage do NOT pay or reimburse the subscription fee itself; a subscription mainly helps people with no Medigap, high Advantage copays, or trips Medicare denies. Medicaid enrollees generally cannot or need not join. REVIEW 2026-10-02: FirstCare page re-read: apply online (application page above), by phone, or mail with check/money order. Membership year runs April 1 - March 31; renewals must be postmarked before April 1 to avoid a gap; new applications after Jan 1, 2027 are not accepted for the current year. No automatic renewal; renew yearly.

entries.name: Hawaii Life Flight membership (AirMedCare Network)
entries.service_area_detail: Hawaii; AMCN reciprocity with other AMCN providers nationwide
entries.senior_programs: $99/yr per household; $79/yr for seniors over 60.
entries.notes: CANCEL/BILLING: the AMCN support page (https://www.airmedcarenetwork.com/support) has a contact form with topics 'I would like to cancel my membership', 'I need to update my personal/billing info' and 'I need replacement membership cards'; member services also at https://www.airmedcarenetwork.com/member-services-guide and 833-819-3454. Hawaii brand page for the AirMedCare Network membership; new memberships start 15 days after the paid application. Billing, renewal and cancel work as for other AMCN brands (see the Air Evac Lifeteam entry). MEDICARE: Part B covers emergency air ambulance only when ground transport would endanger the patient (80% after the deductible). Since 2022 the No Surprises Act caps out-of-network AIR ambulance cost-sharing at in-network levels for private/group plans, which reduces the value of air memberships for many people; Medicare does not pay the membership fee. REVIEW 2026-10-02: The general AMCN terms page fetched on review does not itself spell out automatic annual renewal (monthly plans recur by nature); confirm auto-renew status and cancel via the support form or 833-819-3454. Standard AMCN terms: memberships are non-refundable except state-specific rules (Wyoming 30-day full refund and pro-rated after; Alaska 15-day cancel window).

entries.payment_processor: Online sign-up on emergenthealth.org; print-and-mail brochure application
entries.senior_programs: $75 per year covers you and dependents; site says it suits seniors without supplemental insurance.
entries.notes: Join any time; membership lasts 12 months from receipt of payment and can be renewed any time. Print/mail application: https://www.emergenthealth.org/wp-content/uploads/2025/01/202410_Member-Plus-Brochure-full.pdf . No auto-renew found. Phone numbers on the page include 734-477-6783 and 269-964-6400 (LifeCare); confirm which handles memberships. MEDICARE: Part B covers medically necessary emergency ground ambulance (80% of the approved amount after the Part B deductible; non-emergency trips only with a doctor's certification); Medigap usually pays the 20%. The federal No Surprises Act does NOT protect against ground-ambulance balance bills. Medicare, Medigap and Medicare Advantage do NOT pay or reimburse the subscription fee itself; a subscription mainly helps people with no Medigap, high Advantage copays, or trips Medicare denies. Medicaid enrollees generally cannot or need not join.

Medicare, Medigap and Medicare Advantage do NOT pay or reimburse the subscription fee itself; a subscription mainly helps people with no Medigap, high Advantage copays, or trips Medicare denies. Medicaid enrollees generally cannot or need not join.

entries.notes: Monthly DPC membership; no insurance billed. MEDICARE: Direct primary care (DPC) practices usually do not bill insurance; to accept a DPC fee from a Medicare patient the physician typically must opt out of Medicare, so neither the DPC fee nor visits there are paid by Medicare, and the patient signs a private contract. entries.name: Wake County EMS $60 Subscription Program (Raleigh, NC)
entries.service_area_detail: All of Wake County; calendar-year subscription
entries.senior_programs: $60 per household per year; requires private insurance or Medicare.
entries.notes: Join online (activation code WAKE) or call 844-239-6690. Sign-up for the next year opens Nov 1; current members get renewal notices in the fall. Terms: https://www.wake.gov/departments-government/emergency-medical-services-ems/60-subscription-program/terms-and-conditions-60-subscription-program . MEDICARE: Part B covers medically necessary emergency ground ambulance (80% of the approved amount after the Part B deductible; non-emergency trips only with a doctor's certification); Medigap usually pays the 20%. The federal No Surprises Act does NOT protect against ground-ambulance balance bills. Medicare, Medigap and Medicare Advantage do NOT pay or reimburse the subscription fee itself; a subscription mainly helps people with no Medigap, high Advantage copays, or trips Medicare denies. Medicaid enrollees generally cannot or need not join. REVIEW 2026-10-02: Page re-read: $60/yr per household; coverage starts two days after payment and ends Dec 31; new sign-ups from Nov 1; current members get renewal notices in the fall (no auto-renew described); emergency 911 transports by Wake County EMS only, not air or non-emergency.

entries.name: Storey County Fire Ambulance Subscription Program (Virginia City, NV)
entries.service_area_detail: Storey County (Virginia City, Lockwood, Mark Twain, TRI Center)
entries.senior_programs: $75 single-subscriber household; $125 households with two or more subscribers (2024-25 rates on page).
entries.notes: New subscriptions and renewals through the EMSecurePay member portal (needs the activation code given by the district). Questions: dedicated membership line 775-847-0954. Ambulance bills: https://storeyfire.org/ambulance-billing . MEDICARE: Part B covers medically necessary emergency ground ambulance (80% of the approved amount after the Part B deductible; non-emergency trips only with a doctor's certification); Medigap usually pays the 20%. The federal No Surprises Act does NOT protect against ground-ambulance balance bills. Medicare, Medigap and Medicare Advantage do NOT pay or reimburse the subscription fee itself; a subscription mainly helps people with no Medigap, high Advantage copays, or trips Medicare denies. Medicaid enrollees generally cannot or need not join. REVIEW 2026-10-02: Page re-read: $75 single-subscriber household / $125 two or more; renew online (EMSecurePay) or email the PDF form to fire@storeycounty.org; excludes nursing/convalescent home residents and people with unpaid past bills. The page text names the "Central Lyon County Fire Protection District service area", which looks like copied wording; confirm coverage area at 775-847-0954.

entries.name: REMSA Health Membership Plus / Care Flight / Sierra Saver (Reno NV)
entries.service_area_detail: Washoe County NV ground (REMSA); Care Flight air over ~50,000 sq mi of NV/CA; Sierra Saver ground plan in Plumas County CA
entries.senior_programs: Premier (ground + air, household) $130/yr; REMSA ground (Washoe only) $90/yr; Care Flight air $75/yr; Sierra Saver (Plumas County ground) $69/yr per household.
entries.notes: Membership Log In and Sign Up are on the Membership Plus page; Sierra Saver signup via https://remsa.formstack.com/forms/membershipform_sierrasaver . Terms: https://www.remsahealth.com/membership-plus-terms-conditions-2/ . Care Flight package is part of the AAMMP reciprocal network. Transport billing: https://www.remsahealth.com/billing-services/ . No auto-renew/cancel page found. MEDICARE: Part B covers medically necessary emergency air ambulance (80% of the approved amount after the Part B deductible); Medigap or a Medicare Advantage plan usually covers most of the rest, and the federal No Surprises Act (2022) bars out-of-network air-ambulance balance billing for insured patients. Medicare does NOT pay for or reimburse the membership fee. Memberships are not insurance and Medicaid enrollees generally may not buy them. Ground part: MEDICARE: Part B covers medically necessary emergency ground ambulance (80% after the Part B deductible; non-emergency trips only with a doctor's certification). Federal No Surprises Act balance-billing protection does NOT apply to ground ambulances, which is what these subscriptions cover (some states have their own laws). Medicare does NOT pay or reimburse the subscription fee. Medicaid enrollees generally may not buy these subscriptions. REVIEW 2026-10-02: Page re-read: Premier $130/yr (ground + regional air, Washoe County household), REMSA Health ground $90, Care Flight air $75, Sierra Saver (Plumas County) $69 via https://remsa.formstack.com/forms/membershipform_sierrasaver. entries.notes: FAQ addresses monthly payment of the membership fee and what is included; member page: https://www.sollishealth.com/for-members . No public cancel/auto-renew page found; contact membership email. MEDICARE: Most concierge physicians stay enrolled in Medicare and bill Medicare/your Medigap or Advantage plan for covered visits, labs and tests as usual. The membership (retainer) fee pays for non-covered extras (longer annual wellness program, access, care coordination) and is NOT covered or reimbursed by Medicare, Medigap or Medicare Advantage. Medicare rules forbid charging the fee for Medicare-covered services themselves.

entries.name: MedFlight Advantage / Advantage Global Membership (Ohio)
entries.parent_company: MedFlight of Ohio (nonprofit; with MedCare Ambulance and AirMed)
entries.service_area_detail: MedFlight service territory in central/southern Ohio (Advantage); Advantage Global adds jet transport anywhere in the US and abroad
entries.senior_programs: Advantage $69.99/yr per household; Advantage Global $269.99 individual / $369.99 family. Eligibility: Ohio residents 18 to 75 (Global: US residents, same age limit), so people over 75 cannot newly enroll.
entries.notes: Sign up: https://medflightadvantage.medflight.com/enrollment/enrollment.aspx ; renew in the member portal. Covers helicopter, mobile ICU and MedCare ground ambulance. Memberships include automatic 'no-hassle' renewal; to turn it off or cancel call 1-855-632-3884 (Mon-Fri 8-5 ET); no self-service cancel page found. Benefits start 72 hours after payment. Medicaid recipients are not eligible; uninsured members get 50% off. Earlier passes recorded MedFlight as having no consumer membership, but this page shows one. MEDICARE: Part B covers emergency air ambulance only when ground transport would endanger the patient (80% after the deductible). Since 2022 the No Surprises Act caps out-of-network AIR ambulance cost-sharing at in-network levels for private/group plans, which reduces the value of air memberships for many people; Medicare does not pay the membership fee. REVIEW 2026-10-02: Membership page re-read: $69.99/yr Advantage (Ohio residents 18-75), Global $269.99 individual / $369.99 family (US residents 18-75); "automatic no-hassle renewal"; benefits start 72 hours after payment. Receipts: if you cannot print one from the portal, email membership@medflight.com. Phone 1-855-632-3884 M-F 8am-5pm ET. Cancel/stop auto-renew: no public page; call or email membership. Medicaid recipients are ineligible. Members over 75 cannot buy this product.

entries.name: CareFlite Caring Hearts Membership (North Texas air + ground)
entries.parent_company: CareFlite (nonprofit; joint venture of 5 hospital systems)
entries.service_area_detail: CareFlite helicopter and ground ambulance service area (Dallas-Fort Worth / North Texas)
entries.phone_customer_service: (972) 339-4243 (membership); membership@careflite.org
entries.senior_programs: $79/yr per household; $49/yr military/first responder. Underinsured/private-pay members get 50% off charges.
entries.notes: Auto-renewal is opt-in: the membership agreement on the membership page says the member must reapply at term end unless the automatic-renewal box is checked (same page for setup; contact membership to stop). Join/renew and manage membership in the eServices membership portal. Membership effective on the date of application and payment; members must keep insurance and dependent info current. CareFlite accepts insurance payment as payment in full for members. Transport bills (not membership) are paid at https://admin.eservicestech.com/expresspay/careflite . Transport billing entry exists in medical-physician-ambulance-billing.json; this entry is the membership. MEDICARE: Part B covers medically necessary emergency air ambulance (80% of the approved amount after the Part B deductible); Medigap or a Medicare Advantage plan usually covers most of the rest, and the federal No Surprises Act (2022) bars out-of-network air-ambulance balance billing for insured patients. Medicare does NOT pay for or reimburse the membership fee. Memberships are not insurance and Medicaid enrollees generally may not buy them. Ground part: MEDICARE: Part B covers medically necessary emergency ground ambulance (80% after the Part B deductible; non-emergency trips only with a doctor's certification). Federal No Surprises Act balance-billing protection does NOT apply to ground ambulances, which is what these subscriptions cover (some states have their own laws). Medicare does NOT pay or reimburse the subscription fee. Medicaid enrollees generally may not buy these subscriptions.

entries.notes: CANCEL/BILLING: the AMCN support page (https://www.airmedcarenetwork.com/support) has a contact form with topics 'I would like to cancel my membership', 'I need to update my personal/billing info' and 'I need replacement membership cards'; member services also at https://www.airmedcarenetwork.com/member-services-guide and 833-819-3454. Brand-level pointer: this provider's membership IS an AirMedCare Network (AMCN) membership; the main AMCN entry is in medical-physician-ambulance-billing.json (airmedcarenetwork.com, renew at https://www.airmedcarenetwork.com/renew/renew-your-membership). Provider page states $99/yr per household, $79/yr for seniors over 60; new memberships start 15 days after completed application and payment. Membership questions: 800-793-0010 or amcn.questions@gmr.net (per Guardian Flight contact block). Review 2026-10-02: AMCN terms list 1/3/5/10-year terms and a MONTHLY option ($9/month standard or senior/affinity; $14.99 Fly-U-Home), so monthly members have a recurring charge; annual senior rate $79, 10-year senior $589. Memberships are non-refundable except state exceptions (e.g., Alaska 15-day withdrawal, Wyoming pro-rated cancellation). AMCN footer: alliance of Air Evac Lifeteam, Guardian Flight, Med-Trans and REACH. AMCN FAQ says Medicaid usually pays air ambulance in full and members certify they are not Medicaid beneficiaries. No public self-service cancel page; call. MEDICARE: Part B covers medically necessary emergency air ambulance (80% of the approved amount after the Part B deductible); Medigap or a Medicare Advantage plan usually covers most of the rest, and the federal No Surprises Act (2022) bars out-of-network air-ambulance balance billing for insured patients. Medicare does NOT pay for or reimburse the membership fee. Memberships are not insurance and Medicaid enrollees generally may not buy them. REVIEW 2026-10-02: The general AMCN terms page fetched on review does not itself spell out automatic annual renewal (monthly plans recur by nature); confirm auto-renew status and cancel via the support form or 833-819-3454. Standard AMCN terms: memberships are non-refundable except state-specific rules (Wyoming 30-day full refund and pro-rated after; Alaska 15-day cancel window).

entries.service_area_detail: GMR air-ambulance brand; membership honored across AMCN providers (~320 bases in 38 states)
entries.phone_customer_service: Membership 800-793-0010; patient accounts 801-938-8200; AirMedCare Network site contact 833-819-3454

entries.notes: CANCEL/BILLING: the AMCN support page (https://www.airmedcarenetwork.com/support) has a contact form with topics 'I would like to cancel my membership', 'I need to update my personal/billing info' and 'I need replacement membership cards'; member services also at https://www.airmedcarenetwork.com/member-services-guide and 833-819-3454. Brand-level pointer: this provider's membership IS an AirMedCare Network (AMCN) membership; the main AMCN entry is in medical-physician-ambulance-billing.json (airmedcarenetwork.com, renew at https://www.airmedcarenetwork.com/renew/renew-your-membership). Provider page states $99/yr per household, $79/yr for seniors over 60; new memberships start 15 days after completed application and payment. Membership questions: 800-793-0010 or amcn.questions@gmr.net (per Guardian Flight contact block). Review 2026-10-02: AMCN terms list 1/3/5/10-year terms and a MONTHLY option ($9/month standard or senior/affinity; $14.99 Fly-U-Home), so monthly members have a recurring charge; annual senior rate $79, 10-year senior $589. Memberships are non-refundable except state exceptions (e.g., Alaska 15-day withdrawal, Wyoming pro-rated cancellation). AMCN footer: alliance of Air Evac Lifeteam, Guardian Flight, Med-Trans and REACH. AMCN FAQ says Medicaid usually pays air ambulance in full and members certify they are not Medicaid beneficiaries. No public self-service cancel page; call. MEDICARE: Part B covers medically necessary emergency air ambulance (80% of the approved amount after the Part B deductible); Medigap or a Medicare Advantage plan usually covers most of the rest, and the federal No Surprises Act (2022) bars out-of-network air-ambulance balance billing for insured patients. Medicare does NOT pay for or reimburse the membership fee. Memberships are not insurance and Medicaid enrollees generally may not buy them. REVIEW 2026-10-02: The general AMCN terms page fetched on review does not itself spell out automatic annual renewal (monthly plans recur by nature); confirm auto-renew status and cancel via the support form or 833-819-3454. Standard AMCN terms: memberships are non-refundable except state-specific rules (Wyoming 30-day full refund and pro-rated after; Alaska 15-day cancel window).

entries.notes: If a senior sees a recurring charge from 'Hint' or a practice name via Hint, it is usually a direct-primary-care membership fee billed by that practice. Hint supports patient-paid memberships, invoicing and point-of-sale for practices; to change payment, get receipts or cancel, contact the practice (Hint is the processor, not the provider). Find DPC practices: DPC Frontier mapper https://mapper.dpcfrontier.com (3,208 mapped practices as of this check). MEDICARE: Direct primary care (DPC) practices usually do not bill insurance; to accept a DPC fee from a Medicare patient the physician typically must opt out of Medicare, so neither the DPC fee nor visits there are paid by Medicare, and the patient signs a private contract. The patient keeps Medicare (Part A/B/D and any Medigap/Advantage) for specialists, hospitals, labs and imaging outside the practice. Since 2026 (2025 law) DPC fees up to $150/month individual can be paid from an HSA, but people enrolled in Medicare cannot contribute to an HSA.

Medicaid enrollees are not billed a balance and do not need a membership. MEDICARE: Part B covers medically necessary emergency air ambulance (80% of the approved amount after the Part B deductible); Medigap or a Medicare Advantage plan usually covers most of the rest, and the federal No Surprises Act (2022) bars out-of-network air-ambulance balance billing for insured patients. Medicare does NOT pay for or reimburse the membership fee. Memberships are not insurance and Medicaid enrollees generally may not buy them.
